note: Every public project in github.com/cyberdudeuk. Summaries are written from each project's own README. Status is as each project states it. tools/discover.py flags any public repository missing from this list.

projects.name: AI Capability Governance and Implementation
projects.summary: Guidance you can act on for governing AI and AI agents in public services: a six-level human review model, evidence and transparency record generators, an agent registry pattern and a weekly signals scan.
projects.audience: Anyone using, buying, approving or assuring AI in public services
highlights: Six-level human review model
Evidence and transparency record generators
Agent registry pattern
Weekly signals scan

projects.name: DCAT-AP-UK
projects.summary: A proposed application profile for describing UK public sector datasets and data services, so they can be found, judged and shared across every catalogue. Under review; the endorsed model remains the cross-government metadata exchange model.
projects.audience: Catalogue owners, metadata leads and data architects

projects.name: Data Asset Management capability playbooks
projects.summary: Step-by-step guidance on data governance, data cataloguing and data quality for critical data assets in UK government, built around the data asset management policy.
projects.audience: Data owners, stewards, catalogue managers and data leaders

projects.name: DAM Policy Explorer
projects.summary: A one-stop shop for the UK government Data Asset Management Policy, made for DAM Policy coordinators and usable by anyone: the policy in plain English, questions and answers, and the return step by step.
projects.audience: DAM Policy coordinators, data owners and stewards, and anyone working on the return

projects.name: Public Sector Data Quality Commons
projects.summary: A free, open hub and toolkit for data quality in the public sector: check data, find the frameworks and standards that apply, learn, use AI safely and share what works.
projects.audience: Anyone responsible for data quality, from first steps to automation

projects.name: OpenGovernment UK
projects.summary: One register of the UK state: every public body the official registers know about, who it answers to, who pays for it and who owns it, with each fact traced to the source it came from.
projects.audience: Anyone who needs to know how a public body fits into the state: researchers, journalists, data teams and civic technologists
highlights: 3,477 public bodies, each traced to source
Accountability chains to an elected body
Funding, PFI contracts and ownership
Open feeds: W3C ORG, DCAT 3, BODS 0.4

projects.name: Starting a business in the UK
projects.summary: Everything you have to do to start a business in the UK, in order: your plan, every step, public body and identifier, the rules your activity triggers, and the four nations, with every claim traced to its source.
projects.audience: People starting a business, the people who advise them, and the teams who design the journey
highlights: A founder's plan, in order
Every step, body and identifier
Four nations and international comparison
953 sources in a verification register

projects.name: GitHub Repos Asset Catalogue
projects.summary: Before you build it, look for it. Every UK public sector code project on GitHub in one place, explained in plain English, so you can find work that already exists and decide whether to reuse it.
projects.audience: Policy leads, service owners, data leaders and engineers

projects.name: Legacy Technology Observatory
projects.summary: The old technology behind UK public services, from COBOL and mainframes to phone lines, emergency radio, devices and encryption: where it runs, what it costs, who can still maintain it, and how to move off it. Every figure links to its source.
projects.audience: Service owners, digital and technology leaders, workforce planners and engineers

projects.name: The Knowledge Web
projects.summary: A navigable, ontology-backed map of a body of work on UK government data standards, governance and knowledge management, delivered as one self-contained file that works offline.
projects.audience: People mapping or navigating a large body of knowledge

projects.name: Plainspoken
projects.summary: A phone-first speaking coach for anyone who speaks at work, with situations drawn from public sector settings: a daily 20-minute routine, event preparation, speak-and-score, role-play and a live cue card.
projects.audience: Anyone who wants to speak more clearly at work
projects.licence: PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0 code (see repository for content)

projects.name: Awards and Recognition Hub
projects.summary: Verified award dates, fair ways to recognise people and teams, and tools to send recognition where people work. A calendar of deadlines and ceremonies for 14 award routes, a finder for which award fits which kind of work, and guidance on everyday recognition. It never submits anything: people always send. Formerly the Recognition Opportunities Portal.
projects.audience: Civil servants and managers in central government deciding whether and how to nominate or recognise colleagues

projects.name: Black History and Heritage Hub
projects.summary: A year-round hub celebrating Black and Black-Mixed history, heritage and cultures, Africa and the African diaspora. Launched as the BHM 2026 Hub for Black History Month 2026 in the UK; every figure links to its source.
projects.audience: Colleagues across the public sector and the wider community

projects.name: NDL PubSec MCP
projects.summary: An open-source, read-only MCP server and portal for finding UK public sector data, APIs, MCP servers and open standards, and for mapping data exchanges between public bodies by citizen and business journey. Explained for people with no technical background, with a feed other portals can harvest.
projects.audience: Government and the wider public sector, researchers, journalists and civil society, organisations in every sector, and developers of AI models and MCP servers

projects.name: UK Youth Parliament: Amplify portal
projects.summary: A youth voice portal: young people's issues, a local routes map, and a dated snapshot of a UK Parliament petition. Public and written for young people.
projects.audience: Young people, and those who work with them

projects.name: Young Person 360º: before the label
projects.summary: Every child and young person the state holds, loses or never sees, across the UK, from birth: who they are, how many there are, the records kept about them, and where the trail breaks. Every figure cites its source.
projects.audience: People who design, run or scrutinise services for children and young people, and young people themselves
highlights: Children held, lost or unseen, from birth
BEET and CHEET: the states before NEET
The record trail and where it breaks
107 checks the page runs on itself

projects.name: Earning, learning and training
projects.summary: For young people aged 16 to 24 who are not in work, learning or training, and everyone around them: what helps, what government is doing about it, and how to get into work, learning, training or your own business. Every claim cites its source.
projects.audience: Young people aged 16 to 24, the people who support them, and the teams who design the services
highlights: 17 routes into work, learning, training or a business
The Milburn Review and every UK strategy that bears on it
Which routes are open in each of the four nations
Formerly Earning or learning

excluded.why: Forks and private repositories are not listed, nor are the repositories that hold the GitHub profile page and the default community files, which are not projects.

ways_in._note: Suggested starting points per level, chosen by the owner. Edit freely.
